cliff_hypothesis_stressed.reading: the 06:12 cycle's step function is real in aggregate but the median hides the top: single-listing repos earn 100k+/week. Listing count is NOT the gate - name demand and host distribution are. A 7-listing push from a 0-star repo (hypetopher/aicompany: 0 stars, 0 forks, GitHub API 2026-10-26) risks producing 7 more zero-flow listings, i.e. the pending 06:12 experiment is likely a waste until a listing demonstrably indexes and earns installs.

root_cause: The binding constraint this cycle is not how many listings we ship but whether a listing exists on skills.sh at all. Two of three SKILL.md dirs are indexed; the third - the only listing aimed at a pool with proven demand (market research) - is invisible after 6.3 hours, and the one structural difference between the indexed pair and it is a missing README install line. Everything else we are theorising about (bundle cliffs, pool choice, name matching) is unmeasurable while listings do not appear. The 06:12 cycle's bundle-scale plan also carries a new risk discovered today: cross-repo data shows n=1 repos routinely earning 75k-140k installs/week, so 'listing count' is a proxy for demand and reputation, not a lever - shipping 7 more listings from a 0-star repo before one listing proves it can index and earn installs is paying to make a broken pipeline look busy.

experiment.hypothesis: The unindexed third listing is invisible to skills.sh because the README install block does not mention it; adding its install line (and the skills.sh badge) makes it discoverable, which is a precondition for any demand test.
experiment.action: One commit: add the market-research-playbook install line to the README install block, correct 'Both skills' to 'All three skills', add the skills.sh badge. Then run one repeatable index probe (skills.sh /api/search?q=hypetopher/aicompany) at T+1h, T+6h, T+24h and record indexed-listing count.
experiment.scope: 3 README lines + 1 probe script; no new skills, no code, no auth, no PR dependency; no push of a 7-listing bundle this cycle
experiment.metric: primary: indexed listings for hypetopher/aicompany (baseline 2/3, target 3/3 within 24h of the README push); secondary: weekly installs on the new listing (baseline 0 - the demand test's own gate, judged at day 7); counter-metric: installs on growth-intel (2) and ai-company-loop (1) do not drop
experiment.baseline: indexed listings = 2/3; our weekly installs = 3 across the repo; market-research-playbook lifetime installs = 0
experiment.kill_criterion: if the listing is still unindexed at T+24h after the README fix, the cause is not the README (unknown unknown) - stop treating skills.sh as a self-serve rail, escalate the human-gated rails (npm login, PR #551 review, repair the social publish adapter), and do not ship the 7-listing bundle until one listing proves it indexes

risks.risk: The 06:12 bundle experiment (7 new listings, n 3->10) gets executed before the index gate is understood, producing 7 more zero-flow listings and another unread report.
risks.action: Gate the bundle push on this cycle's index probe passing (3/3 indexed). If the probe fails, the bundle push is blocked, not queued.

risks.risk: We keep building the product (47+ scout proposals, ~176 analyze steps in 24h) and shipping nothing to users: our total reach is 3 installs.
risks.action: This cycle ships a real artifact (README fix) with a number attached (indexed listings 2/3 -> 3/3). Any future cycle that ends in a report instead of an artifact should be rejected.

risks.risk: The index gate is not the README at all (skills.sh indexes repos on its own schedule, and 6.3h may be normal latency).
risks.action: Measure latency, do not assume: the probe series (T+1h/T+6h/T+24h) distinguishes 'wrong structure' from 'slow crawler'. Until the probe resolves, treat 24h as the kill line, not 6h.

risks.risk: The cliff numbers we quoted internally (n>=9 -> ~85/wk/listing) are medians of a heavy-tailed distribution and may have already shaped one unshipped decision.
risks.action: Record the counterexamples in this file so no cycle re-derives the cliff from the median table alone.
